verses.pali: Tatra kho āyasmā ānando bhikkhū āmantesi:
“Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa paccassosuṁ.
“Puṇṇo nāma, āvuso, āyasmā mantāṇiputto amhākaṁ navakānaṁ sataṁ bahūpakāro hoti.
verses.english: “Reverends, the venerable named Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī was very helpful to me when I was just ordained.

verses.pali: ‘upādāya, āvuso ānanda, asmīti hoti, no anupādāya.
verses.english: ‘Reverend Ānanda, the thought “I am” occurs because of grasping, not without grasping.

verses.pali: Kiñca upādāya asmīti hoti, no anupādāya?
Rūpaṁ upādāya asmīti hoti, no anupādāya.
verses.english: The thought “I am” occurs because of grasping form,

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ upādāya asmīti hoti, no anupādāya.
Seyyathāpi, āvuso ānanda, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udakapatte sakaṁ mukhanimittaṁ paccavekkhamāno upādāya passeyya, no anupādāya;
verses.english: Suppose there was a woman or man who was young, youthful, and fond of adornments, and they check their own reflection in a clean bright mirror or a clear bowl of water. They’d look because of grasping, not without grasping.

verses.pali: evameva kho, āvuso ānanda, rūpaṁ upādāya asmīti hoti, no anupādāya.
verses.english: In the same way, the thought “I am” occurs because of grasping form,

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ upādāya asmīti hoti, no anupādāya.

verses.english: What do you think, Reverend Ānanda?
They understand: “… there is nothing further for this place.”’

verses.pali: Puṇṇo nāma, āvuso, āyasmā mantāṇiputto amhākaṁ navakānaṁ sataṁ bahūpakāro hoti.
verses.english: Reverends, the venerable named Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī was very helpful to me when I was just ordained.

verses.pali: Idañca pana me āyasmato puṇṇassa mantāṇiputtassa dhammadesanaṁ sutvā dhammo abhisamito”ti.
verses.english: And when I heard this teaching from Venerable Puṇṇa son of Mantāṇī, I comprehended the teaching.”
